searchText: <@425274498732916736> creating a thread here - against the finalised (and frozen) upgrade spec. the point would be to formally establish that the client impl of the hard fork correctly implements the specified state transition and consensus rules, rather than merely relying on tests & cross-client agreement. ofc this also raises the harder q of how we gain confidence that the spec itself is correct, but i see impl-to-spec verification as a meaningful first step. maybe we could consider Geth as the ground truth spec? then what's the point of the formal verification? we can just fork whenever Geth says to fork and just use geth
